paras: The Third Ward polling-place assaults took place on 3 June 1882 at the Third Ward polls in Wilmington, Delaware, during a municipal election, when a crowd of Democrats drove colored voters from the polls and beat two men who vouched for them. Mr. Burchall was badly beaten and Edmund Mitchell nearly killed, according to the Republican Daily Republican, the only paper found to report the assaults.

The city election of Saturday, 3 June, pitted a Republican ticket headed by Dr. J. P. Wales against the Democrats, and the Republicans won the mayoralty by about 150 votes. In its ward-by-ward report, the Daily Republican charged that Democratic election officers had tried to stuff ballot boxes and to keep qualified Republicans from voting, and it described disputes over colored voters in several wards.

In the Third Ward, the paper said, the Democratic Inspector, Henry Witsil, "assisted by a gang of Democrats on the outside," kept hundreds of colored voters from casting ballots, and a colored man had no chance to vote unless he was "well attended." When Burchall, a foreman at the Pulp Works, came up to vouch for a colored man, he was set upon by the crowd and badly beaten. Edmund Mitchell was beaten for the same cause and "came very near losing his life" trying to see that an entitled voter got his vote.

Colored men who presented themselves were "hustled and bullied" until they were glad to escape, and one resident who was turned away was then "pounced upon" by police officers, where the surviving text breaks off. The paper also accused Witsil of hurrying in challenged ballots and swearing in young men "on age," and it counted only 880 votes cast out of 1,300 voters in the ward.

No arrest or prosecution of the Third Ward assailants appears in the coverage. When the new City Council organized on 6 June, Republicans contested an Eleventh Ward result with charges that ruffians had kept Republicans "white and colored" from the polls, but no Third Ward contest was reported.

The assaults appeared only in the Daily Republican, which placed them among the "outrages upon Republican voters" and argued that a fair election in the ward would have swelled the Republican majority. A Wilmington dispatch in the Washington National Republican gave only the returns. The Democratic Daily Gazette, by contrast, mocked the Republican victory parade under the headline "REPUBLICAN ORGIE," dwelling on the "blacks" in the crowd, and did not mention the violence at the polls.

bases: A Democratic crowd at the Third Ward polls beat two men who vouched for colored voters and drove colored voters away, as part of an effort to keep them from voting (A3).

accounts.label: Republican paper's election report
accounts.gist: Inspector Witsil and a gang of Democrats kept hundreds of colored voters from voting; Burchall and Mitchell were beaten for vouching for them, and colored men were bullied until they fled.

framing.detail: The Republican Daily Republican listed the beatings among 'outrages upon Republican voters' and said a fair election would have swelled the Republican majority.
The Washington National Republican's Wilmington dispatch gave only the returns.
The Democratic Daily Gazette ridiculed the Republican victory parade as a 'REPUBLICAN ORGIE' of 'blacks' and whites, without mention of the polling-place violence.
